```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Lu_2017_pictilisib"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Lu_2017_pictilisib"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1002/psp4.12228> (open access, PMC5702897)
* Supplement: the NONMEM control stream of the final population PK model
  (Supporting Information, plain-text file) and Tables S1-S4.

Lu 2017 combines a "top-down" population PK analysis with a "bottom-up"
GastroPlus PBPK model to explain the effect of a high-fat meal and of the
proton-pump inhibitor (PPI) rabeprazole on the absorption of the weakly basic
PI3K inhibitor pictilisib. This article packages the population PK model.
The PBPK model is a GastroPlus (ACAT) platform model whose equations are not
published; see "Assumptions and deviations".

# Population

The model was fitted to 1,202 plasma concentrations from 31 healthy
volunteers in a single-center, four-period, two-sequence, open-label,
randomized crossover study (NCT00999128). Every subject received a single
40 mg pictilisib dose in each of four periods: fasted, fed (standard high-fat
meal within 30 min of dosing), fasted after 4 days of rabeprazole 20 mg daily,
and fed after rabeprazole. Lu 2017 does not tabulate the volunteers'
demographics (the clinical study is reported in Ware et al., Mol Pharm
2013;10:4074-4081), and no demographic covariate enters the model.

```{r population}
readModelDb("Lu_2017_pictilisib")()$population
```

# Source trace

Every `ini()` value carries an in-file comment naming its source. Table 1 of
Lu 2017 holds the final estimates; the supplementary NONMEM control stream
(final-model run, `$TABLE ... FILE=RES22`, matching run 22 of Table S3)
fixes the equation forms but carries initial estimates only.

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|----------------------|-------|-----------------|
| `lcl` (CL/F, fasted, no PPI) | log(26.0) L/h | Table 1 'Clearance (CL/F)' and its footnote |
| `lvc` (Vc/F) | log(304.9) L | Table 1 'Central volume (Vc/F)' |
| `lq` (Q/F) | log(13.9) L/h | Table 1 'Distribution clearance (Q/F)' |
| `lvp` (Vp/F) | log(175.9) L | Table 1 'Peripheral volume (Vp/F)' |
| `lka` (fasted, no PPI) | log(2.63) 1/h | Table 1 'Ka, PPI=0, Fasted' |
| `e_fed_ka` | log(0.297 / 2.63) = -2.181 | Table 1 'Ka, PPI=0, Fed' / 'Ka, PPI=0, Fasted' |
| `e_conmed_ppi_ka` | log(1.361 / 2.63) = -0.659 | Table 1 'Ka, PPI=1, Fasted' / 'Ka, PPI=0, Fasted' |
| `ltlag` | log(0.47) h | Table 1 'Absorption lag time (Tlag)' |
| `lfdepot` | fixed(log(1)) | Table 1 'F, PPI=0, Fasted' = 100%; control stream THETA(8) '1 FIX' |
| `e_conmed_ppi_f` | -0.571 | Table 1 'F, PPI=1, Fasted' = 42.9% |
| `e_fed_f` | 0.184 | Table 1 'F, PPI=0, Fed' = 118.4% |
| `etalcl`, `etalvc` | 0.230^2, 0.377^2 | Table 1 BSV 23.0%, 37.7% |
| `etalka` | 0.519^2 | Table 1 BSV 51.9% (shared by all four states) |
| `etaltlag` | 0.030^2 | Table 1 BSV 3.00% |
| `etalfdepot_fasted` / `_fastedppi` / `_fed` / `_fedppi` | 0.27^2 / 0.64^2 / 0.089^2 / 0.32^2 | Table 1 F BSV 27% / 64% / 8.9% / 32%; Results text |
| `expSd` | 0.561 | Table 1 'Residual error (proportional)' 56.1% |
| `ka = exp(lka + e_fed_ka*FED + e_conmed_ppi_ka*CONMED_PPI + etalka)` | n/a | control stream `KA=EXP(THETA(5)+THETA(7)*FOOD+THETA(9)*PPI+ETA(6))` |
| `fdepot = (1 + e_conmed_ppi_f*CONMED_PPI + e_fed_f*FED) * exp(eta_f)` | n/a | control stream `F1 = (THETA(8)+THETA(10)*PPI+THETA(11)*FOOD)*EXP(FETA)` |
| `eta_f` selects one of four etas by state | n/a | control stream `FETA=ETA(7)*OCC1+ETA(8)*OCC2+ETA(9)*OCC3+ETA(10)*OCC4` |
| Two-compartment disposition, lag on depot | n/a | Results 'two-compartment model with first-order absorption with lag time'; control stream `ADVAN4 TRANS4`, `ALAG1` |
| `Cc = 1000 * central / vc` (ng/mL) | n/a | control stream `S2=V2/1000`, `;CONC IN NG/ML`, `;AMT IN mg` |
| `Cc ~ lnorm(expSd)` | n/a | Methods 'additive error model on the log-transformed data'; control stream `Y=IPRED+EPS(1)`, `IPRED=LOG(F)` |

The model's typical relative bioavailability and absorption rate in each
state reproduce every row of Table 1:

```{r table1-check}
mod <- readModelDb("Lu_2017_pictilisib")
p <- rxode2::rxode(mod)$theta
states <- tibble::tibble(
  state = c("Fasted", "Fasted with PPI", "Fed", "Fed with PPI"),
  FED = c(0, 0, 1, 1),
  CONMED_PPI = c(0, 1, 0, 1),
  ka_table1 = c(2.63, 1.361, 0.297, 0.154),
  f_table1 = c(1.000, 0.429, 1.184, 0.613)
) |>
  mutate(
    ka_model = exp(p[["lka"]] + p[["e_fed_ka"]] * FED + p[["e_conmed_ppi_ka"]] * CONMED_PPI),
    f_model = exp(p[["lfdepot"]]) + p[["e_conmed_ppi_f"]] * CONMED_PPI + p[["e_fed_f"]] * FED
  )
# Ka for fed with PPI is the one value not used to derive a coefficient, so
# it is an independent check of the log-additive form; F for fed with PPI
# checks the additive form.
stopifnot(
  max(abs(states$ka_model / states$ka_table1 - 1)) < 0.005,
  max(abs(states$f_model - states$f_table1)) < 1e-9
)
states |>
  dplyr::select(state, ka_table1, ka_model, f_table1, f_model) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "State" = state,
    "Ka, Table 1 (1/h)" = ka_table1,
    "Ka, model (1/h)" = ka_model,
    "F, Table 1" = f_table1,
    "F, model" = f_model
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3, caption = "Typical Ka and relative bioavailability by state.")
```

# Virtual cohort

The four study periods are simulated as four arms of 150 virtual subjects
each, with disjoint subject IDs. Because each subject in the source study
met each state exactly once, the state-specific bioavailability etas are
drawn once per subject per state either way; the arm design simply does not
carry a subject's CL/F, Vc/F and Ka etas across periods, which does not
change the per-state distributions that the paper's VPC summarises.

```{r cohort}
set.seed(20170825)
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20170825)

n_per_arm <- 150L
obs_times <- sort(unique(c(
  seq(0, 2, by = 0.25), seq(2.5, 12, by = 0.5), seq(13, 24, by = 1),
  seq(26, 72, by = 2)
)))

make_arm <- function(state, fed, ppi, id_offset) {
  ids <- id_offset + seq_len(n_per_arm)
  dose <- tibble(
    id = ids, time = 0, amt = 40, evid = 1L, cmt = "depot"
  )
  obs <- tidyr::expand_grid(id = ids, time = obs_times) |>
    mutate(amt = 0, evid = 0L, cmt = "central")
  bind_rows(dose, obs) |>
    mutate(state = state, FED = fed, CONMED_PPI = ppi) |>
    arrange(id, time, desc(evid))
}

state_levels <- c("Fasted", "Fasted with PPI", "Fed", "Fed with PPI")
events <- bind_rows(
  make_arm("Fasted", 0, 0, 0L),
  make_arm("Fasted with PPI", 0, 1, 1000L),
  make_arm("Fed", 1, 0, 2000L),
  make_arm("Fed with PPI", 1, 1, 3000L)
)
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(unique(events[, c("id", "time", "evid")])))
```

# Simulation

```{r simulate}
sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  mod,
  events = events,
  keep = c("state", "FED", "CONMED_PPI"),
  returnType = "data.frame"
) |>
  mutate(state = factor(state, levels = state_levels))

sim_typ <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  rxode2::zeroRe(mod),
  events = events |> dplyr::filter(id %in% c(1L, 1001L, 2001L, 3001L)),
  keep = c("state"),
  returnType = "data.frame"
) |>
  mutate(state = factor(state, levels = state_levels))
```

# Replicate published figures

## Figure 3 (top four panels): VPC by state

```{r figure-3-vpc, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 6}
vpc <- sim |>
  dplyr::filter(time > 0) |>
  group_by(state, time) |>
  summarise(
    Q05 = quantile(Cc, 0.05, na.rm = TRUE),
    Q50 = quantile(Cc, 0.50, na.rm = TRUE),
    Q95 = quantile(Cc, 0.95, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

ggplot(vpc, aes(time, Q50)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = Q05, ymax = Q95), fill = "lightskyblue", alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_line(colour = "firebrick") +
  geom_line(data = sim_typ |> dplyr::filter(time > 0), aes(time, Cc), linetype = "dashed") +
  facet_wrap(~state) +
  scale_y_log10(limits = c(0.1, 1000)) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 72, by = 6)) +
  labs(
    x = "Time (h)", y = "Plasma pictilisib concentration (ng/mL)",
    title = "Simulated 5th-95th percentile band and median after 40 mg",
    caption = paste(
      "Replicates the VPC panels of Figure 3 of Lu 2017 (observations not",
      "available). Dashed: typical-value profile."
    )
  )
```

The typical profiles peak at about 112 ng/mL (fasted, 1.7 h), 44 ng/mL
(fasted with PPI, 2.4 h), 83 ng/mL (fed, 5.7 h) and 33 ng/mL (fed with PPI,
8.1 h) (table in the PKNCA section), close to the model medians drawn in the
source figure (about 100, 40, 70-80 and 30 ng/mL), and the 5th-95th
percentile band spans roughly 1-7 ng/mL at 72 h, as there.

## Figure 3 (bottom panels): individual F and Ka by state

```{r figure-3-box, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 3.5}
indiv <- sim |>
  group_by(id, state) |>
  summarise(F = 100 * first(fdepot), Ka = first(ka), .groups = "drop") |>
  pivot_longer(c(F, Ka), names_to = "parameter", values_to = "value") |>
  mutate(parameter = factor(parameter,
    levels = c("F", "Ka"),
    labels = c("Relative bioavailability F (%)", "Absorption rate constant Ka (1/h)")
  ))

ggplot(indiv, aes(state, value)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.size = 0.5) +
  facet_wrap(~parameter, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(
    x = NULL, y = NULL,
    caption = paste(
      "Replicates the boxplots of Figure 3 of Lu 2017 (the paper plots",
      "post hoc estimates of the 31 subjects; these are simulated draws)."
    )
  ) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 20, hjust = 1))
```

# PKNCA validation

```{r pknca}
sim_nca <- sim |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, Cc, state)
sim_nca <- bind_rows(
  sim_nca,
  sim_nca |> distinct(id, state) |> mutate(time = 0, Cc = 0)
) |>
  distinct(id, state, time, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  arrange(id, state, time)

dose_df <- events |>
  dplyr::filter(evid == 1) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, amt, state)

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(sim_nca, Cc ~ time | state + id)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_df, amt ~ time | state + id)
intervals <- data.frame(
  start = 0, end = Inf,
  cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE, aucinf.obs = TRUE, half.life = TRUE
)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))
```

## Typical-value AUC identity

For the typical subject in each state, `AUC(0-inf) = 1000 * Dose * F / (CL/F)`
in ng*h/mL. A deterministic solve on a fine grid run out to 600 h (about 34
terminal half-lives) must reproduce it; the remaining difference is
trapezoidal error.

```{r auc-identity}
typ_times <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, 12, by = 0.05), seq(12.5, 600, by = 0.5))))
typ_events <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_along(state_levels), function(i) {
  fed <- c(0, 0, 1, 1)[i]
  ppi <- c(0, 1, 0, 1)[i]
  bind_rows(
    tibble(id = i, time = 0, amt = 40, evid = 1L, cmt = "depot"),
    tibble(id = i, time = typ_times, amt = 0, evid = 0L, cmt = "central")
  ) |>
    mutate(state = state_levels[i], FED = fed, CONMED_PPI = ppi)
}))
typ <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  rxode2::zeroRe(mod),
  events = typ_events, keep = "state", returnType = "data.frame",
  rtol = 1e-10, atol = 1e-12
)
auc_typ <- typ |>
  group_by(state) |>
  summarise(auc_trap = sum(diff(time) * (head(Cc, -1) + tail(Cc, -1)) / 2), .groups = "drop") |>
  left_join(states |> dplyr::select(state, f_table1), by = "state") |>
  mutate(auc_closed = 1000 * 40 * f_table1 / exp(p[["lcl"]]))
# Measured difference about 0.01% (linear trapezoids on a 0.05 h grid).
stopifnot(max(abs(auc_typ$auc_trap / auc_typ$auc_closed - 1)) < 0.005)
auc_typ |>
  dplyr::select(state, f_table1, auc_closed, auc_trap) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "State" = state, "F" = f_table1,
    "AUC0-inf, 1000*Dose*F/CL (ng*h/mL)" = auc_closed,
    "AUC0-inf, solve (ng*h/mL)" = auc_trap
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = c(0, 3, 1, 1))

# Typical-value Cmax and Tmax by state, from the same deterministic solve.
typ |>
  group_by(state) |>
  summarise(Cmax = max(Cc), Tmax = time[which.max(Cc)], .groups = "drop") |>
  dplyr::rename("State" = state, "Typical Cmax (ng/mL)" = Cmax, "Typical Tmax (h)" = Tmax) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = c(0, 1, 2))
```

## Comparison against published NCA

Lu 2017 reports the median AUCinf (1,760, 2,070, 906 and 1,180 ng*h/mL) and
median Tmax (2, 4, 2 and 6 h) for fasted, fed, fasted with PPI and fed with
PPI (Results, 'Results of the clinical pharmacology study'; from the
noncompartmental analysis of Ware 2013). `ncaComparisonTable()` summarises the
simulated subjects by their median.

```{r nca-compare}
published <- tibble::tribble(
  ~state, ~aucinf.obs, ~tmax,
  "Fasted", 1760, 2,
  "Fasted with PPI", 906, 2,
  "Fed", 2070, 4,
  "Fed with PPI", 1180, 6
)
cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = nca_res,
  reference = published,
  by = "state",
  units = c(aucinf.obs = "ng*h/mL", tmax = "h"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)
knitr::kable(cmp, caption = "Simulated (median) vs. published (median) NCA. * differs by more than 20%.")
```

```{r nca-gate}
sim_auc <- as.data.frame(nca_res) |>
  dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD == "aucinf.obs") |>
  group_by(state) |>
  summarise(med = median(PPORRES, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
  left_join(published, by = "state") |>
  mutate(ratio = med / aucinf.obs)
# Structural gate on the centre only. The model-true median AUCinf is the
# typical 1538 * F ng*h/mL (13-27% below the published NCA medians, see
# the narrative). With 150 subjects per arm the SD of log AUC is at most
# about 0.68 (fasted with PPI), so the sample median carries about 7% error;
# a mis-transcribed CL/F, F or dose moves the ratio far outside 0.55-1.10.
stopifnot(all(sim_auc$ratio > 0.55), all(sim_auc$ratio < 1.10))
```

The model's median AUCinf in each state is the typical
`1000 * 40 * F / 26.0` ng*h/mL (1,538, 660, 1,822 and 943 ng*h/mL; table
above), which is 13% (fasted), 27% (fasted with PPI), 12% (fed) and 20% (fed
with PPI) below the published NCA medians. The simulated sample medians
scatter around those values by sampling error, most in the fasted-with-PPI
arm, where the SD of log AUC is about 0.68 and 150 subjects leave the median
uncertain by roughly 7% (one standard error), so the flagged difference in
that row can exceed the 27% structural offset. The **relative** food and PPI effects
agree with the observations: the model's fed / fasted ratio is 1.18 against
an observed 1.18 (2,070 / 1,760), and its PPI ratios are 0.43 (fasted) and
0.52 (fed) against observed 0.51 and 0.57. The model's CL/F and F are its
final estimates and are not adjusted. The absolute offset is the difference
between the NONMEM fit and a noncompartmental summary of the same 31
subjects; Lu 2017 does not report model-based AUCs to compare against.

The model reproduces the direction and rough size of the food delay in Tmax
(typical 1.7 h fasted versus 5.7 h fed), but its Tmax in the two fed states
falls later than the observed medians of 4 and 6 h (typical 5.7 and 8.1 h),
and the typical fasted-with-PPI Tmax (2.4 h) is slightly later than the
observed 2 h. A
single first-order absorption with one lag time cannot reproduce the
segmented gastric emptying that the authors' PBPK analysis attributes the
fed-state profile to (Figure 1c, Table 2); the source VPC (Figure 3) shows
the same flat, late fed-state median.

# Assumptions and deviations

- **Population PK model only.** The PBPK half of Lu 2017 is a GastroPlus 8.5
  ACAT model (Johnson dissolution, segmented stomach transit time and pH
  for the fed states, Table 2 and Appendix S1; drug properties in Table
  S1). GastroPlus's ACAT equations, its PEAR physiology and its default
  fasted/fed physiologies are not published in the paper, so that model
  cannot be reproduced from the source and is not packaged.
- **BSV convention.** Table 1 reports BSV as percentages without stating
  the transformation. They are read as `omega = BSV/100` on the log scale
  (`omega^2 = (BSV/100)^2`), the convention under which the same table's
  log-scale residual SD reads as 56.1%. Under the alternative
  `omega^2 = log(1 + CV^2)` every variance would be 2-4% smaller, except for
  F fasted with PPI (0.343 instead of 0.410).
- **CL/F-Vc/F correlation omitted.** Table S3 retains a CL/F-Vc/F OMEGA
  block (`base model with BLOCK(CL,Vc)`, -2LL drop 25.2), but Table 1 does
  not report the final covariance or correlation, and the control stream
  carries only initial estimates. The two etas are therefore independent
  here. This does not change typical profiles or AUC (AUC depends on CL/F
  only) but narrows the spread of early concentrations slightly.
- **Covariate coefficients derived from Table 1.** Table 1 reports Ka and F
  per state rather than the THETAs. The log-additive Ka coefficients are the
  log ratios of the fasted rows, and the additive F coefficients are the
  differences from 100%; the fed-with-PPI rows, which were not used, are
  reproduced to within 0.4% (Ka) and exactly (F). The Results text says Ka
  'decreased by ~80% with food'; Table 1 gives 89% (2.63 to 0.297), and the
  table values are used.
- **Bioavailability between-subject variability by state.** The control
  stream applies one of four etas to F1 according to the food/PPI state of
  the period (Table S3 'IOV on F1'). Each subject met each state once, so
  the four etas act as state-specific between-subject variability and are
  implemented as four subject-level etas selected by `FED` and
  `CONMED_PPI`. The Ka eta is shared by all four states, as in the control
  stream.
- **Residual error.** The paper fits log-transformed concentrations with an
  additive error, labelled 'proportional' in Table 1; it is encoded as a
  log-normal error with SD 0.561.
- **Covariates.** The source columns `FOOD` and `PPI` map to the canonical
  `FED` and `CONMED_PPI`. Fed means a standard high-fat meal within 30 min
  of dosing; PPI means rabeprazole 20 mg daily for 4 days before dosing.
- **No demographic data.** Lu 2017 does not report age, weight, sex or race
  of the 31 volunteers, and the model has no demographic covariate.
- **Errata.** No correction notice for Lu 2017 was found in Europe PMC as of
  2026-11-25.
